rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **What it is:** a balanced critical evaluation — what the work is, what it does well, what falls short, and whether it is worth the reader's time.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Trick 1: Review anatomy: title/creator → one-line premise (no spoilers) → two strengths → one weakness → verdict with a rating — the five-part frame.
Trick 2: Judge against PURPOSE, not taste: a thriller must thrill, a documentary must inform — state the criterion before judging.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Never spoil the ending** — restraint reads as mature judgement.  ·  **Full guide:** Full model answers, starting-line banks and exam tips: [/knowledge/writing](/knowledge/writing).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Q. Write a short review of a film you have recently watched. (4 marks) — premise, one strength with example, one weakness, verdict.

rows.label: Solved

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **What it is:** a balanced critical evaluation — what the work is, what it does well, what falls short, and whether it is worth the reader's time.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Structure:** Title + basic details (title, author/director, year, genre) → Brief SPOILER-FREE summary (2–3 sentences) → Strengths (one concrete example/quote) → Weaknesses (fair, with why it matters) → Recommendation + verdict/rating.  ·  **Review grammar:** present simple dominates ('the story follows…'); evaluative adjectives (compelling, uneven, luminous); concessive fairness ('although the plot is thin, the philosophy is profound'); soft hedging ('readers may find…').

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 3: Use the vocabulary bank: plot, pacing, characterisation, cinematography, narrative arc — technical terms lift the band instantly.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. What must a review avoid? (1 mark) — major spoilers and purely personal bias without criteria.
